description:
## Problem
The 2026-10-07 addendum in `docs/development/tuning-adr-003-baseline-and-single-renderer.md` (section "Addendum (2026-10-07): ClickHouse TPC-H tuned run slower than baseline") claims more than its evidence shows:
1. "a partition has no pruning benefit at any scale for these tables, so there is no tier to select". Only SF1 was measured. Partitioning also changes part counts, merges and parallelism, which depend on scale.
2. "Its slowest queries were Q3 (1.49×) and Q5 (1.44×), because `lineitem` is no longer ordered by order key". The TPC-H table row repeats the "because". The study data does not support a cause: Q3 read 0.54× the rows yet took 1.43× the time; Q5 read 0.84× and took 1.49×; Q10 read 0.42× and took 1.00×.
3. The sentence with "ran at 0.79× the baseline geometric mean" does not mention that Q21 is excluded. Q21 fails at the 5.25 GiB envelope without its per-query hash override, so it was left out of the 21-query study.
4. The TPC-DS row says "The same three queries fail in every cell." The bundles show one query, Q10, failing all three measured iterations and the warm-up with "memory limit exceeded ... maximum: 4.67 GiB", in all three cells.
5. The SSB and TPC-DS rule ("within about 10%") was chosen after the numbers were seen. The Keep decisions rest on single sequential CLI cells at SF1.
6. The merge-settle wait runs only after tuned server loads (`benchbox/platforms/clickhouse/workload.py:665`). `notuning` cells may therefore time queries while merges still run, which favours tuned.

## Change
Edit only the wording of that addendum:
- Scope the partitioning conclusion to SF1, ClickHouse 25.8 and the 5.25 GiB envelope. List SF10+ as unmeasured and point to `clickhouse-tpch-layout-study-sf10-plus`.
- Remove every causal "because" for Q3, Q5 and Q18. State the rows-read and time ratios, and mark the cause unproven, pointing to `clickhouse-tpch-q3-q5-slowdown-probe-20261008`.
- Put the Q21 exclusion in the same sentence as the 0.79× figure.
- Name Q10 as the one failing TPC-DS query.
- Mark the per-template decisions as provisional and SF1-only until the benefit rule (`tuning-evidence-benefit-rule-20261008`) exists. Say that the SSB and TPC-DS threshold was set after measurement.
- State the tuned-only settle asymmetry until `tuning-evidence-merge-settle-recorded-20261008` resolves it.

## Decision gate
- Read how earlier ADR-3 addenda record corrections. If they amend in place, amend in place. If not, append a dated "Correction" section that quotes each superseded sentence. Either way, the original claim must stay traceable.

## Guardrails (must preserve)
- Docs only. Do not change any decision: the template contents, the session pack contents and the Q21 override all stay.
- Every number added must come from the bundle or study file named in context. Do not re-derive numbers from memory.
- Plain English (ISO 24495-1). Keep session labels, such as finding IDs and reviewer names, out of the ADR text.

## Process guardrails
- One PR per item against `develop`, via the AGENTS.md worktree flow (`make worktree-claim BRANCH=...`, `make agent-write-preflight`).
- Verification ladder: `uv run -- python -m pytest -m fast -q`, `uv run -- ruff check .`, `uv run -- ruff format --check .` and `uv run -- ty check`. Then `make pr-preflight` and `make pr-open`.
- Stage explicit paths; never `git add -A`.
- Re-read every file:line anchor before editing. Anchors are from develop 5ca12e6ca.
